suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(metafor))

# dat.bcg: 13 trials of the BCG vaccine against tuberculosis (Colditz et al. 1994).
main <- function(inputs, report, run) {
  outputs <- list()
  d <- escalc(measure = "RR", ai = tpos, bi = tneg, ci = cpos, di = cneg, data = dat.bcg)
  d <- as.data.frame(d)
  d$yi <- as.numeric(d$yi)
  d$vi <- as.numeric(d$vi)
  file <- file.path(run$output_directory, "bcg.csv")
  write.csv(d, file, row.names = FALSE)
  outputs[["trials"]] <- list(value = file)
  report$table(data.frame(
    Trial = d$trial, Author = d$author, Year = d$year,
    Vaccinated = sprintf("%d / %s", d$tpos, format(d$tpos + d$tneg, trim = TRUE)),
    Control = sprintf("%d / %s", d$cpos, format(d$cpos + d$cneg, trim = TRUE)),
    Latitude = d$ablat, RR = sprintf("%.2f", exp(d$yi)), `log RR` = sprintf("%.3f", d$yi), Variance = sprintf("%.4f", d$vi),
    check.names = FALSE))

  outputs
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(metafor))

# Fixed and random effects pooling, and the forest plot with both diamonds.
main <- function(inputs, report, run) {
  outputs <- list()
  method <- inputs$params$method
  excluded <- unlist(inputs$params$exclude)
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("trials"))
  d <- d[!d$trial %in% excluded, ]
  fixed <- rma(yi, vi, data = d, method = "EE")
  random <- rma(yi, vi, data = d, method = method)
  rows <- rbind(
    data.frame(model = "fixed", method = "EE", k = fixed$k, estimate = as.numeric(coef(fixed)), se = fixed$se,
               rr = exp(as.numeric(coef(fixed))), lower = exp(fixed$ci.lb), upper = exp(fixed$ci.ub), tau2 = 0, I2 = fixed$I2, Q = fixed$QE),
    data.frame(model = "random", method = method, k = random$k, estimate = as.numeric(coef(random)), se = random$se,
               rr = exp(as.numeric(coef(random))), lower = exp(random$ci.lb), upper = exp(random$ci.ub), tau2 = random$tau2, I2 = random$I2, Q = random$QE))
  file <- file.path(run$output_directory, "pooled.csv")
  write.csv(rows, file, row.names = FALSE)
  outputs[["pooled"]] <- list(value = file)
  report$log(paste(capture.output(print(rows)), collapse = "\n"))
  labels <- sprintf("%s, %d", d$author, d$year)
  k <- nrow(d)
  report$figure({
    par(mar = c(4, 0, 2.6, 0), cex = 0.95)
    forest(random, slab = labels, atransf = exp, at = log(c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)), xlim = c(-7.2, 4.4), alim = log(c(0.1, 4)),
           ylim = c(-2.5, k + 3), addfit = FALSE, xlab = "Risk ratio (log axis)",
           header = c("Trial", "RR [95% CI]"))
    addpoly(fixed, row = -1, mlab = "Fixed effect (EE)", atransf = exp)
    addpoly(random, row = -2, mlab = sprintf("Random effects (%s)", method), atransf = exp)
    abline(h = 0)
    title(sprintf("BCG vaccine, %d trials: I² = %.1f%%, τ² = %.3f, Q = %.1f", k, random$I2, random$tau2, random$QE), font.main = 1)
  }, alt = sprintf("Forest plot with fixed %.3f and random %.3f pooled risk ratios", rows$rr[1], rows$rr[2]), width = 8.5, height = 5.6)

  outputs
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(metafor))

# Funnel plot, Egger-type regression and trim and fill.
main <- function(inputs, report) {
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("trials"))
  model <- rma(yi, vi, data = d, method = inputs$params$method)
  egger <- regtest(model)
  filled <- trimfill(model)
  report$log(paste0(sprintf("regtest z %.3f p %.3f; trim and fill adds %d, RR %.3f", egger$zval, egger$pval, filled$k0, exp(as.numeric(coef(filled))))))
  report$figure({
    par(mar = c(4.4, 4.4, 3.4, 1))
    funnel(model, atransf = exp, at = log(c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)), xlab = "Risk ratio (log axis)", ylab = "Standard error", pch = 19, back = "grey95", shade = "grey95")
    title(sprintf("I² = %.1f%%, τ² = %.3f\nregression test p = %.2f, trials added by trim and fill %d", model$I2, model$tau2, egger$pval, filled$k0), font.main = 1, cex.main = 1)
  }, alt = sprintf("Funnel plot, regression test p %.2f", egger$pval), width = 6.4, height = 5)

  invisible(NULL)
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(metafor))
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# Meta-regression: does the effect change with the moderator?
main <- function(inputs, report, run) {
  outputs <- list()
  name <- inputs$params$moderator
  method <- inputs$params$method
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("trials"))
  d$x <- d[[name]]
  overall <- rma(yi, vi, data = d, method = method)
  m <- rma(yi, vi, mods = ~ x, data = d, method = method)
  rows <- data.frame(moderator = name, method = method, intercept = coef(m)[1], slope = coef(m)[2], slope_se = m$se[2],
                     QM = m$QM, QM_p = m$QMp, tau2 = m$tau2, tau2_without = overall$tau2, R2 = m$R2, I2 = m$I2)
  file <- file.path(run$output_directory, "regression.csv")
  write.csv(rows, file, row.names = FALSE)
  outputs[["regression"]] <- list(value = file)
  report$log(paste(capture.output(print(rows)), collapse = "\n"))
  grid <- seq(min(d$x), max(d$x), length.out = 100)
  band <- as.data.frame(predict(m, newmods = grid))
  band$x <- grid
  d$weight <- weights(m)
  figure <- ggplot(d, aes(x, yi)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(x, ymin = ci.lb, ymax = ci.ub), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_line(data = band, aes(x, pred), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(aes(size = weight), colour = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.75, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text_repel(aes(label = trial), size = 3.4, colour = "grey20", box.padding = 0.55, seed = 1, min.segment.length = Inf) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 9) +
    scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(transform = exp, name = "Risk ratio", breaks = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2))) +
    labs(x = if (name == "ablat") "Absolute latitude of the trial site (degrees)" else name, y = "log risk ratio",
         title = sprintf("Slope %.4f (p = %.2g). τ² %.3f → %.3f, proportion explained R² = %.0f%%", m$b[2], m$pval[2], overall$tau2, m$tau2, m$R2),
         subtitle = "Point size is the weight, numbers are trial numbers, the band is the 95% confidence interval") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
  report$figure(print(figure), alt = sprintf("Meta-regression on %s, slope %.4f", name, m$b[2]), width = 7.5, height = 5)

  outputs
}

outputs.note: CSV of the pooled values by trial left out and by estimator

files.text:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(metafor))
library(ggplot2)

# What moves the pooled estimate: dropping one trial, or changing the tau^2 estimator.
main <- function(inputs, report, run) {
  outputs <- list()
  d <- read.csv(inputs$path("trials"))
  methods <- inputs$params$estimators
  fit <- function(x, method) {
    m <- rma(yi, vi, data = x, method = method)
    data.frame(rr = exp(as.numeric(coef(m))), lower = exp(m$ci.lb), upper = exp(m$ci.ub), tau2 = m$tau2, I2 = m$I2)
  }
  loo <- function(method, label) do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i)
    cbind(panel = label, name = sprintf("%2d %s", d$trial[i], d$author[i]), left_out = d$trial[i], fit(d[-i, ], method))))
  leave <- rbind(loo("EE", "Leaving one trial out: fixed effect"), loo("DL", "Leaving one trial out: random effects DL"))
  estimators <- do.call(rbind, lapply(methods, function(k) cbind(panel = "Changing the estimator (all trials)", name = k, left_out = NA, fit(d, k))))
  rows <- rbind(leave, estimators)
  file <- file.path(run$output_directory, "sensitivity.csv")
  write.csv(rows, file, row.names = FALSE)
  outputs[["sensitivity"]] <- list(value = file)

  full <- data.frame(panel = c("Leaving one trial out: fixed effect", "Leaving one trial out: random effects DL"), rr = c(fit(d, "EE")$rr, fit(d, "DL")$rr))
  span <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(x$rr), max(x$rr))
  names_order <- c(rev(unique(leave$name)), rev(methods))
  rows$name <- factor(rows$name, levels = names_order)
  rows$panel <- factor(rows$panel, levels = c(full$panel, "Changing the estimator (all trials)"))
  figure <- ggplot(rows, aes(rr, name)) +
    geom_vline(data = full, aes(xintercept = rr), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0, orientation = "y", colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 1.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Pooled risk ratio (log axis; lines are 95% confidence intervals, the dashed line is the value with all trials)", y = NULL,
         title = sprintf("How far the pooled risk ratio moves: leaving one out (fixed effect) %s, leaving one out (random effects) %s, estimators %s",
                         span(leave[leave$panel == full$panel[1], ]), span(leave[leave$panel == full$panel[2], ]), span(estimators))) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  report$figure(print(figure), alt = "Leave-one-out and estimator comparison of the pooled risk ratio", width = 10, height = 4.8)

  outputs
}

notes.html:
Meta-analysis: the BCG vaccine and tuberculosis

The data is dat.bcg, bundled with metafor: real data from 13 clinical trials of the BCG vaccine against tuberculosis (Colditz et al., JAMA 1994;271:698–702).

Each trial's log risk ratio yiy_i and its variance viv_i are pooled with weights wiw_i.

μ^=∑iwiyi∑iwi,wi=1vi+τ2\hat\mu=\frac{\sum_i w_i y_i}{\sum_i w_i},\qquad w_i=\frac{1}{v_i+\tau^2}

τ2=0\tau^2=0 is the fixed effect; allowing for heterogeneity between trials, τ2>0\tau^2>0, is random effects. I2I^2 is the share of the total variation taken by the differences between trials.

moderator is the known explanation, a meta-regression on the latitude of the trial sites (the further from the equator, the larger the effect). It is an observational association at the level of trials, though, and latitude itself cannot be called the cause.

Change method (DL, REML, ...) and exclude (trial numbers to leave out) of pool and rerun just that Card. sensitivity lays out the change when one trial is left out and when the estimator changes.

An example of statistical methods for old trials, not advice about vaccination.
